introduction.greeting: We sincerely welcome all of you who have visited the Guri Cult Counseling Center website.

paragraphs.text: The Guri Cult Counseling Center is a counseling center affiliated with Chodae Church of the Presbyterian Church of Korea (Hapdong) denomination and is a member of the Korean Christian Cult Counseling Association. Our center provides counseling and prevention ministry to help individuals, families, and churches who are experiencing difficulties due to Shincheonji.

The most distinctive feature of the Guri Cult Counseling Center is that all of our counseling ministers have personally experienced Shincheonji for more than 10 years. With this unique background, all ministers have gathered with a heart of repentance and a sense of mission, making this a specialized Shincheonji counseling center. Led by Director Pastor Hyun-wook Shin, our full-time counseling ministers strive to provide practical help for recovery and healing based on their real experience with Shincheonji and years of counseling ministry.
highlights: all of our counseling ministers have personally experienced Shincheonji for more than 10 years

paragraphs.text: The Guri Cult Counseling Center has been conducting counseling and prevention activities primarily offline. However, with the hope that more people can access accurate information about Shincheonji and receive the help they need, we have created this website.

While information about Shincheonji has been available through various channels, the sheer volume of information has sometimes made it difficult to find what is actually needed. Therefore, this website focuses on systematically organizing Shincheonji-related materials and counseling information so that anyone can more easily understand and utilize them.

We hope this website will serve as an opportunity for those struggling within Shincheonji to discern the truth and move toward recovery. We hope it will be a channel of comfort and courage for affected families in their overwhelming situations, and practical help for churches and believers in prevention and response.
highlights: an opportunity for those struggling within Shincheonji to discern the truth and move toward recovery
a channel of comfort and courage for affected families in their overwhelming situations
practical help for churches and believers in prevention and response

paragraphs.text: The Guri Cult Counseling Center will continue to do its best to be a counseling center that values each soul and helps with recovery and healing in the truth.

introduction.closing: We bless all who visit this website with the abundant grace and love of the Lord.

sections.heading: 1. If You Are a Shincheonji Member

items.title: Investigating is not a sin (e.g., Thomas)
items.description: Jesus did not condemn Thomas as a sinner, but personally showed him the nail marks in His hands (John 20:27).

items.title: The chairman himself said to verify.
items.description: Is merely questioning Shincheonji the forbidden fruit? Can even past Shincheonji materials be forbidden fruit?

items.title: Examine the evidence and fulfillment according to Deuteronomy 18:20-22
items.description: 2 Corinthians 11:14 - An angel of light disguises itself; a con artist never admits to being one. Satan is the one who cuts off communication and sows discord, seeking to place himself in God's seat (Ezekiel 28 / Matthew 23:2).

items.title: Who are the seven demons?
items.description: Things get worse by joining Shincheonji, not by leaving it.

sections.heading: 2. If a Family Member or Friend Is in Shincheonji

items.title: Do not panic
items.description: They are still our friends, family, and fellow human beings. The sensational portrayals in the media represent only a part; excessive worry can escalate the situation and cloud your judgment.

items.title: Never hastily attempt religious counseling — doctrinal discussions will not get through
items.description: Many cases exist where people underestimated the situation and tried to resolve it carelessly, only to push the person deeper into Shincheonji.

items.title: First, secure solid evidence that they are in Shincheonji
items.description: Without concrete evidence, they will hide the truth with lies.

items.title: Based on evidence, assess how much of their life is kept secret
items.description: Even within Shincheonji, the degree of commitment varies; you can roughly gauge their involvement by how much Shincheonji work they do.

items.title: Show genuine love — not the false, legalistic love of Shincheonji — starting from family and friends
items.description: Simply leaving Shincheonji is not everything; how they live after leaving and their recovery is what truly matters.

items.title: Even when attempting dialogue, build trust with family/friends first
items.description: Never blame, mock, or look down on them. Approach with respect and suggest verifying things together.

items.title: Most claims about monetary demands or negative counseling methods from Shincheonji are not true
items.description: Casual counseling is possible anywhere — at a cafe or any setting. Coercive methods are no longer used except in truly necessary cases.

paragraphs.text: Sadly, not all Shincheonji members believe they are saved in the name of Jesus. What distinguishes them from orthodox churches is that they believe salvation comes through Jesus' new name — that is, the name of Man-hee Lee.
highlights: they believe salvation comes through Jesus' new name — that is, the name of Man-hee Lee

paragraphs.text: Furthermore, Shincheonji members believe that even though their own physical immortality is not guaranteed before the union of spirit and flesh, Man-hee Lee himself will never die physically and will live forever. They believe he is the Advocate (Paraclete). Yet Man-hee Lee himself has stated in court and in public, 'I never said I was the Advocate, I never said I wouldn't die, there is no savior other than Jesus' — such blatant contradictions push the limits of patience for any person of faith.
highlights: I never said I was the Advocate, I never said I wouldn't die, there is no savior other than Jesus

paragraphs.text: When I think of Shincheonji members who are blind to a few Bible verses and have gone all in with their lives without knowing the true nature of Man-hee Lee — especially the members of Saebit Church that I pioneered and pastored, and among them the ministers who serve faithfully from dawn to late night without properly caring for their families — my heart aches with regret and sorrow, and tears blur my vision.

Thankfully, by the grace of God, after many twists and turns, I came to see that Man-hee Lee is not the promised true shepherd, but rather the false Christ and false prophet prophesied for the last days. I was able to experience the overwhelming joy and gratitude of salvation by restoring our Lord Jesus Christ to the throne I had once given over to Man-hee Lee. Hallelujah!
highlights: the false Christ and false prophet prophesied for the last days
restoring our Lord Jesus Christ to the throne

paragraphs.text: I spent my golden years — my twenties and thirties, when I should have been learning and preparing with the most passion both spiritually and in the world — blinded by mere zeal to know the Bible, losing discernment, deceived by Man-hee Lee, and wasting my life. I was furious and resentful, blaming myself and falling into despair.

However, with the conviction that there should be no more victims like me, with a desire to atone for my sins as a chief of sinners, and with a heavy sense of responsibility, I declare a holy war against Man-hee Lee. I resolve to devote the life that has been given back to me to the faith recovery movement of turning pitiful Shincheonji members back to Jesus, and to the ministry of combating the many cults that pose a serious threat to the Korean church.

toMembersContent.emphasis: Let me emphasize once more at this time.
toMembersContent.closing:
The reality of Shincheonji is a thoroughly fabricated illusion — a patchwork imitation made from doctrines that Man-hee Lee himself was deceived by as he wandered through numerous cults. The fact is that Man-hee Lee will absolutely never live forever in the flesh. My earnest prayer is that Shincheonji members, even after the death of their leader, will not seek another savior, another recipient of revelation, another overcomer, or another Advocate, but will return to Jesus Christ — the one and only eternal Savior testified by the Bible.

Just as in the parable of the prodigal son, where one must leave home to know the preciousness of parents and family, the experience of Shincheonji is undoubtedly a deep wound — yet because of it, I came to realize even more deeply how warm and precious the embrace of our Lord, our first love, truly is.

I urge all believers: when you encounter victims who have been led astray by cults and enslaved to vanity, please remember that before they are targets of condemnation and criticism, they are lost sheep and prodigal children who have left home. Please pray for them with the Lord's compassionate heart, and when they come to their senses and return, embrace them warmly with love.

And I pray in the name of the Lord that you will guard your faith and your church with a strong sense of ownership, armed with the Word, and achieve revival and growth as healthy believers in healthy churches.

historyContent.intro: Shincheonji Church of Jesus, the Temple of the Tabernacle of the Testimony (commonly abbreviated as 'Shincheonji') is a religious organization founded by Lee Man-hee in 1984. Its headquarters is in Gwacheon, Gyeonggi Province, which adherents believe to be the place where 'a new heaven and a new earth'—Shincheonji—is realized. Lee Man-hee was born in 1931 in Cheongdo, Gyeongsangbuk-do, and at the age of 27, joined the Olive Tree Movement (Korean Jesus Church Evangelism Revival Association) founded by Park Tae-sun, originally seeking treatment for Hansen's disease (leprosy). After learning Park Tae-sun's doctrines there, Lee went on to join Yoo Jae-yeol's Tabernacle Temple and Gu In-hoe's Heavenly Gospel Evangelism Association before eventually creating Shincheonji. Perhaps because of this, Shincheonji bears striking similarities to these groups.

paragraphs.text: Park Tae-sun is known to have studied the Bible under Kim Baek-mun, a mystical sect leader, alongside Moon Sun-myung of the Unification Church. Park Tae-sun, who died in 1990, established the Olive Tree Movement in 1955 and gathered followers through unique doctrines inherited from Kim Baek-mun and miraculous signs such as 'divine healing.' In 1980, he revised his doctrines and renamed the organization Cheonbuism. Followers lived communally in settlements called 'Faith Villages' and operated businesses producing socks, cosmetics, food products, and more. Around the 1960s–70s, Park caused major social controversies through forced consumption of 'Holy Water (Water of Life)' and 'Zion Caramel' manufactured in the Faith Village under the pretext of divine healing—leading to follower deaths—as well as charges of promiscuity based on the so-called 'Blood Sharing (spiritual-physical union)' doctrine, fraud, perjury, and assault.
highlights: charges of promiscuity based on the so-called 'Blood Sharing (spiritual-physical union)' doctrine, fraud, perjury, and assault

paragraphs.text: In 1957, Lee Man-hee entered this Faith Village and lived there for 10 years, following Park Tae-sun who called himself God. He then joined the 'Tabernacle Temple' in Gwacheon, Gyeonggi Province in 1967. Yoo Jae-yeol, also from the Olive Tree Movement, established the Tabernacle Temple in 1966 and proclaimed the end of the world in 1969, which failed to materialize. According to the Dong-A Ilbo dated April 3, 1975, Yoo relocated followers en masse to Cheonggyesan Mountain in Gwacheon, built a church and luxury homes using their labor, and was reported to the police by some followers for immoral conduct with female members. Yoo was eventually arrested on fraud charges in September of the same year.

Afterward, Lee Man-hee followed Mok Yeong-deuk, a former Unification Church lecturer, and then Baek Man-bong. Baek had broken away from Yoo Jae-yeol at the Tabernacle Temple and established the Recreation Church, causing controversy by claiming March 13, 1980, would be the day of the apocalypse, along with about 100 followers.
highlights: claiming March 13, 1980, would be the day of the apocalypse

paragraphs.text: When nothing happened on Baek Man-bong's proclaimed day of the apocalypse, Lee Man-hee fought with Baek, left with some followers, and began holding worship services at his own home. In September 1980, he was arrested for defamation after publicly criticizing Yoo Jae-yeol. After his release in February 1981, he began meeting with a small group of followers, claiming that the 'Two Witnesses'—representing Moses and Elijah—were Shin Gwang-il and Lee Man-hee. He later changed this claim to Shin Jong-hwan and Lee Man-hee, then reversed it again to Hong Jong-hyo and Lee Man-hee. After parting ways with Hong Jong-hyo as well, Lee elevated himself to the status of Moses. He then claimed to be an apostle with John's mission before gradually upgrading his status to the Advocate (Paraclete) Holy Spirit.
highlights: gradually upgrading his status to the Advocate (Paraclete) Holy Spirit

paragraphs.text: In 1984, he appointed his followers as the 7 Spirits, 12 Apostles, and 24 Elders, and launched Shincheonji.

As outlined above, Lee Man-hee learned the Bible from various figures including Park Tae-sun of Cheonbuism, Yoo Jae-yeol of the Tabernacle Temple, Gu In-hoe of the Heavenly Gospel Evangelism Association, Mok Yeong-deuk from the Unification Church, and Baek Man-bong of the Recreation Church.

Not only the 'Divine-Human Unity' doctrine—a modification of the 'Blood Sharing (spiritual-physical union)' doctrine—but also the headquarters location in Gwacheon, Gyeonggi Province, the use of 'Tabernacle Temple' in the organization's name, and the 12-Tribe organizational structure all share the same lineage. Currently, Shincheonji members employ unconventional methods for their proselytization activities.
highlights: 'Divine-Human Unity' doctrine—a modification of the 'Blood Sharing (spiritual-physical union)' doctrine

paragraphs.text: These include the so-called 'Harvester Strategy' and 'Mountain Moving Strategy.' The Harvester Strategy involves covertly registering at other churches (called 'harvest fields') and luring their members away. The Mountain Moving Strategy similarly involves covertly joining another church, then seducing the pastor to take over the entire church.
The number of followers is estimated at approximately 240,000 to 250,000 (as of 2025).
